sources.entry: Gokapi - Lightweight server to share files, which expire after a set amount of downloads or days. Similar to the discontinued Firefox Send, with the difference that only the admin is allowed to upload files. GPL-3.0 Go/Docker
Gokapi | Lightweight file sharing with expiring links

summary.one_liner: Gokapi is a self-hosted, lightweight file-sharing server written in Go, where shared files expire after a set number of downloads or days.
summary.what_it_does: Gokapi lets you share files through links that expire automatically after a set number of downloads or a set number of days. It is described as a self-hosted alternative to Firefox Send. Only registered users can upload, and user management supports roles for finer permission control. External parties can upload via a file request URL, and those uploads are visible only to the URL's creator. Identical files are deduplicated so they use no extra space. Storage can be local or an optional S3-compatible backend such as AWS S3 or Backblaze B2. It also offers built-in encryption including end-to-end encrypted uploads, OpenID Connect login (e.g. Authelia or Keycloak), a REST API, and customizable UI via custom CSS and JavaScript.
use_cases: share large files with others using expiring links
let outside people upload files to me via a request link
file sharing with single sign-on via OpenID Connect
store shared files on S3 or Backblaze B2
automate file sharing through a REST API
how_to_run: docker run --rm --name gokapi -v gokapi-data:/app/data -v gokapi-config:/app/config -p 127.0.0.1:53842:53842 -e TZ=UTC docker.io/f0rc3/gokapi:latest
Open the Gokapi web interface and follow the setup wizard
notable: Expiring shares limited by download count or days
File requests let outside parties upload into the admin's account without user access
File deduplication so identical files take no extra space
OpenID Connect integration with identity providers
caveats: Only registered users can upload, by design (uploads are admin/user controlled)
Recommended SSD storage; minimum 256 MB RAM
S3 support is optional and requires an external S3-compatible service
